notes: Official sites textbooksonline.tn.nic.in and textbookcorp.tn.gov.in could not be read: WebFetch was refused by their robots.txt, and the shell has no internet access. dge.tn.gov.in and tnschools.gov.in were not reached either. The chapter and section titles were therefore taken from copies of the official SCERT/Government of Tamil Nadu textbook PDFs hosted on cdn1.byjus.com (and, for Grade 11 Vol I, on 11thstudymaterials.wordpress.com). These are mirrors of the government PDF (cover 'GOVERNMENT OF TAMIL NADU', '(c) SCERT', 'A publication under Free Textbook Programme') and were used only because the official host was unreachable.

Section titles are the top-level numbered sections from each volume's contents page, as reported by the fetch tool. Capitalisation follows the printed contents, which is inconsistent in the book itself. The fetched PDF text had OCR/ligature artefacts (e.g. 'Th eorem'), so small punctuation or capitalisation differences are possible. Sub-sections (e.g. 1.2.1) are omitted because they could not be seen for every chapter.

Edition for 2026-27: the books in use are still the 'Published under New Syllabus' set (first edition 2018 for Std XI, 2019 for Std XII, with later revised editions). News reports (DT Next, updated 16 Aug 2026; Madhyamam, 6 Nov 2025) say new textbooks under the Tamil Nadu State Education Policy 2025 are being prepared for 2027-28. I found no sign that new Std XI or XII mathematics books were issued for 2026-27. Annual reprints may carry a later reprint year that I could not see.

Reduced syllabus: TN cut the syllabus for the COVID-affected years (2020-21 onward). I found no reduced-syllabus or deleted-portions notice for 2026-27 from DGE or SCERT. Secondary syllabus listings (shaalaa.com, careers360) show the full 12-chapter syllabus for 2026-27. This could not be confirmed on dge.tn.gov.in.

Business Mathematics and Statistics (Std XI and XII, 2 volumes each) is a separate Higher Secondary subject taken in commerce streams. It shares some chapter names (e.g. 'Applications of Matrices and Determinants') but is not inventoried here. Only the Mathematics (core) textbook is covered.
Outcomes are written in my own words from the section structure. They are not official TN learning outcomes: I found no separate official learning-outcomes document for Higher Secondary mathematics.
The existing competencies were written to NCERT grade bands. Some TN placements differ, and mappings follow the skill, not the grade label.

Std XII Vol II contents list section 9.3 'Fundamental Theorems of Integral Calculus and their Applications' and section 9.4 'Bernoulli's Formula'. Some secondary syllabus pages omit these. The textbook contents page was followed.
Std XII Vol I: section lists match between First Edition 2019 and Revised Edition 2020. For Vol II only the revised (2020) contents were seen.

Chapter 11 has no section on Poisson or normal distributions in the contents seen. Only the one-point, two-point, Bernoulli and binomial distributions are listed. This was inferred from the section titles and a secondary syllabus listing, not checked against the body text.
The textbook prints recommended teaching months next to chapters (e.g. Chapter 7 'October'). These were not recorded.

Several Std XII TN topics are absent from the NCERT-based competency list: rank and consistency, de Moivre, theory of equations, triple products, MVT, L'Hopital, Taylor series, partial derivatives, improper and gamma integrals, volumes of revolution, continuous random variables, the binomial distribution, binary operations and propositional logic. New competencies are proposed only for these.

sections.title: 1.2 Inverse of a Non-Singular Square Matrix
1.4 Applications of Matrices: Solving System of Linear Equations
1.5 Applications of Matrices: Consistency of system of linear equations by rank method

outcomes.statement: Find the adjoint and inverse of a non-singular square matrix and use properties of inverses and adjoints.

competencies.why: The 2 × 2 inverse and the 3 × 3 adjoint are computed there; the 3 × 3 inverse is the new family auinv.

outcomes.statement: Apply matrices to geometric transformations (e.g. rotations, orthogonal matrices) and to simple encoding and decoding of messages.
Use elementary row operations to reduce a matrix to row-echelon form, find its rank and find inverses by the Gauss-Jordan method.

proposed.name: Reduce matrices to echelon form and find rank
proposed.why: algebra.matrices covers operations; elementary row/column operations, row-echelon form, rank and Gauss-Jordan inversion are not covered by any competency.

outcomes.statement: Model a situation as a system of linear equations and solve it by matrix inversion, Cramer's rule or Gaussian elimination.
Decide by comparing ranks whether a non-homogeneous system has a unique solution, infinitely many solutions or none, and find the solution set.

proposed.name: Test consistency of linear systems by the rank method
proposed.why: algebra.matrix-systems solves square non-singular systems; classifying systems (unique / infinitely many / no solution, non-trivial homogeneous solutions) via rank comparison is a separate skill.

outcomes.statement: Determine when a homogeneous system has non-trivial solutions and find them, including parameter values that make a system consistent.

proposed.name: Test consistency of linear systems by the rank method
proposed.why: algebra.matrix-systems solves square non-singular systems; classifying systems (unique / infinitely many / no solution, non-trivial homogeneous solutions) via rank comparison is a separate skill.

sections.title: 2.3 Basic Algebraic Properties of Complex Numbers
2.6 Geometry and Locus of Complex Numbers
2.7 Polar and Euler form of a Complex Number
2.8 de Moivre's Theorem and its Applications

outcomes.statement: Perform arithmetic with complex numbers, including powers of i, and represent them in the Argand plane.
Use properties of conjugate and modulus, including the triangle inequality, and find square roots of complex numbers.
Interpret equations and inequalities in z as loci or regions (circles, lines, perpendicular bisectors) in the complex plane.

proposed.name: Describe loci and regions in the complex plane
proposed.why: number.complex covers arithmetic and representation; interpreting conditions such as |z - z0| = r or |z - a| = |z - b| as curves in the Argand plane is not covered.

outcomes.statement: Convert complex numbers between rectangular, polar and Euler forms and multiply or divide in polar form.

competencies.why: asarg (principal argument, the step to polar/Euler form) and aspolm (multiplying and dividing in polar form) assess exactly the missing part; the outcome is mapped only to MATH.number.complex.

outcomes.statement: Use de Moivre's theorem to compute powers, find nth roots of a complex number and solve equations involving roots of unity.

proposed.name: Apply de Moivre's theorem and find nth roots
proposed.why: No existing competency covers powers of complex numbers in polar/Euler form, nth roots of a complex number or roots of unity.

sections.title: 3.3 Vieta's Formulae and Formation of Polynomial Equations
3.4 Nature of Roots and Nature of Coefficients of Polynomial Equations
3.6 Roots of Higher Degree Polynomial Equations
3.8 Polynomial Equations with no additional information

outcomes.statement: Relate the roots and coefficients of polynomial equations using Vieta's formulae, and form equations with given or transformed roots.

proposed.name: Relate roots and coefficients of polynomial equations
proposed.why: Existing polynomial competencies stop at remainder/factor theorem and quadratic zeros; Vieta's formulae for degree n and forming equations from given roots are not covered.

outcomes.statement: Use the conjugate-pair theorems for imaginary and surd roots and the nature of coefficients to deduce remaining roots.

proposed.name: Determine the nature and number of roots of a polynomial
proposed.why: quadratic-discriminant is degree 2 only; Descartes' rule of signs and reasoning about real/imaginary/rational/irrational roots of higher-degree polynomials are absent.

outcomes.statement: Solve higher-degree polynomial equations using additional information such as roots in progression, partial factorisation or coefficient sums.

proposed.name: Solve higher-degree polynomial equations using structure
proposed.why: No competency covers solving cubic/quartic equations using conjugate-root pairs, rational root theorem, roots in progression or reciprocal equations.

outcomes.statement: Solve polynomial equations without extra information using the rational root theorem, reciprocal equations and reducible non-polynomial equations.

proposed.name: Solve higher-degree polynomial equations using structure
proposed.why: No competency covers solving cubic/quartic equations using conjugate-root pairs, rational root theorem, roots in progression or reciprocal equations.

outcomes.statement: Use polynomial equations to solve geometric problems such as finding dimensions satisfying volume or area conditions.

proposed.name: Solve higher-degree polynomial equations using structure
proposed.why: No competency covers solving cubic/quartic equations using conjugate-root pairs, rational root theorem, roots in progression or reciprocal equations.

outcomes.statement: Apply Descartes' rule of signs to bound the numbers of positive, negative and non-real roots.

proposed.name: Determine the nature and number of roots of a polynomial
proposed.why: quadratic-discriminant is degree 2 only; Descartes' rule of signs and reasoning about real/imaginary/rational/irrational roots of higher-degree polynomials are absent.

sections.title: 4.3 Sine Function and Inverse Sine Function
4.4 The Cosine Function and Inverse Cosine Function
4.5 The Tangent Function and the Inverse Tangent Function
4.6 The Cosecant Function and the Inverse Cosecant Function
4.7 The Secant Function and Inverse Secant Function
4.8 The Cotangent Function and the Inverse Cotangent Function

outcomes.statement: Use domain, range, period and amplitude to describe graphs of trigonometric functions and explain why restrictions are needed for inverses.
State domains and ranges of the six inverse trigonometric functions and sketch their graphs.
Find principal values of inverse trigonometric expressions.
Apply properties of inverse trigonometric functions, such as sum formulae and composition rules, to simplify expressions, prove results and solve equations.
Find the equation of a circle from given conditions, its centre and radius from the general equation, and the position of a point relative to it.
Derive and use standard equations of parabola, ellipse and hyperbola from focus-directrix-eccentricity, finding vertices, foci, axes, latus rectum and directrices.
Identify the type of conic represented by a general second-degree equation.
Write parametric equations of conics and find equations of tangents and normals to circles and conics, including the condition for y = mx + c to be a tangent.

proposed.name: Find tangents and normals to circles and conics
proposed.why: coordinate.conics covers standard forms and features; equations of tangents/normals to conics (incl. parametric points and the tangency condition y = mx + c) are not covered.

outcomes.statement: Model real-life situations such as arches, reflectors, orbits and cables with conics and solve for required measurements.

sections.title: 6.7 Different forms of Equation of a Straight line
6.8 Different forms of Equation of a plane
6.9 Image of a point in a plane
6.10 Meeting point of a line and a plane

outcomes.statement: Use dot and cross products to prove geometric and trigonometric results and to compute work done and torque.
Compute scalar and vector triple products, interpret them as volume and coplanarity tests, and apply Lagrange's and Jacobi's identities.

proposed.name: Use scalar and vector triple products
proposed.why: vectors.products covers dot and cross products; scalar triple product (volume, coplanarity), vector triple product and related identities are not covered.

outcomes.statement: Write vector and Cartesian equations of lines in space; find the angle between lines, their point of intersection and the shortest distance between skew or parallel lines.

competencies.why: The shortest distance between skew lines and between parallel lines is asked by asskew and asparl3, in a competency the outcome is not mapped to; the equations of lines and their point of intersection are new families asleq and asint3 in MATH.coordinate.space-lines.

outcomes.statement: Write equations of planes in normal, intercept and point forms, through three points or containing given lines, and find angles and distances involving planes.
Find the image of a point in a plane and the point where a line meets a plane.
Use derivatives as rates of change, solve related-rates problems, and find tangents, normals and angles between curves.
Verify the hypotheses of Rolle's theorem and Lagrange's mean value theorem and apply them to find guaranteed points or prove inequalities.

proposed.name: Apply Rolle's and Lagrange's mean value theorems
proposed.why: No existing competency covers the hypotheses and conclusions of Rolle's theorem and Lagrange's MVT or their use.

outcomes.statement: Obtain Taylor and Maclaurin series expansions of standard functions.

proposed.name: Expand functions as Taylor and Maclaurin series
proposed.why: No existing competency covers generating power-series expansions from derivatives.

outcomes.statement: Evaluate indeterminate forms using l'Hopital's rule, including exponential forms.

proposed.name: Evaluate indeterminate forms using l'Hopital's rule
proposed.why: calculus.limits is elementary limits; using derivatives for 0/0, infinity/infinity and exponential indeterminate forms is not covered.

outcomes.statement: Find intervals of monotonicity and local and absolute extrema using the first and second derivative tests.
Solve optimisation problems arising in geometry and real-life contexts.
Determine concavity, points of inflection, symmetry and asymptotes and use them to sketch curves.

proposed.name: Sketch curves using derivatives, symmetry and asymptotes
proposed.why: calculus.applications covers rates and extrema; concavity, inflection points, asymptotes and assembling a full sketch are not covered.

proposed.name: Use differentials for linear approximation and error estimates

sections.title: 9.2 Definite Integral as the Limit of a Sum
9.3 Fundamental Theorems of Integral Calculus and their Applications
9.8 Evaluation of Bounded Plane Area by Integration
9.9 Volume of a Solid obtained by Revolving Area about an Axis

outcomes.statement: Approximate and evaluate definite integrals as limits of Riemann sums.
Evaluate definite integrals using the fundamental theorems and properties of definite integrals, including Bernoulli's formula.
Evaluate improper integrals and use the gamma integral.

proposed.name: Evaluate improper integrals and gamma integrals
proposed.why: calculus.definite-integrals covers finite intervals; integrals over unbounded intervals and the gamma function are not covered.

outcomes.statement: Apply reduction formulae to evaluate integrals of powers of trigonometric functions and related forms.

outcomes.statement: Find areas bounded by curves and the axes or between two curves.
Find volumes of solids generated by revolving a region about a coordinate axis.

proposed.name: Find volumes of solids of revolution by integration

competencies.why: aqd2rel already asks for the differential equation y″ + py′ + qy = 0 obtained by eliminating the arbitrary constants A and B from a two-constant family; the outcome is only mapped to MATH.calculus.differential-equations.

outcomes.statement: Verify general and particular solutions and solve variables-separable equations and those reducible to it by substitution.

competencies.why: aqhom solves homogeneous first-order equations with y = vx; the outcome is not mapped to that competency.

proposed.why: calculus.differential-equations covers solving given equations; setting up and interpreting ODE models (population growth, radioactive decay, Newton's law of cooling, mixtures) is a separate skill.
